description: From the fz-kdt.130 refutation: ir_interp/backend.rs:~969 builds closure-call continuations from dest and IGNORES return_flow entirely, while native reads return_flow -- which is why the interp was right on 130's byte-identical backend program and also why the interp CANNOT see the dropped-continuation class by construction. Two doors reading different fields of one instruction is a parity hazard: either the interp honors return_flow (and the fz-kdt.130 fixtures would have been red on THREE doors), or the field's authority is documented as native-only with the interp's dest-reading justified. Decide and align.
title: The interpreter ignores return_flow: one instruction, two readings, and a door constitutionally blind to a bug class
